subject: ACME RAG eval - post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acme.com>, Priya Iyer <priya.iyer@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-15T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: ACME RAG eval - post-call recap & next steps

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and recommended next steps so we keep momentum: 

What we heard:
- Primary goal: provide reliable, grounded answers for internal knowledge base search and customer support flows (short answers + citations).
- Current pain: hallucinations on out-of-domain KBs, inconsistent citation coverage, and long-tail latency spikes during peak hours.
- Success metrics: precision@1 for top-1 answer, grounding rate (percent answers with verifiable citations), and end-to-end 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for inline responses.

Initial recommendations (model + infra):
1) Model candidates:
   - Small/fast baseline: LLaMA-2-13B (quantized) for inexpensive filtering & short-answer generation.
   - Production candidate: RedLlama-70B-q4 (Redwood-verified) for higher-accuracy grounding where latency budget allows.
   - Reranker / cross-encoder: USE a compact cross-encoder fine-tuned on your FAQ/KB (we recommend starting with a 3-epoch fine-tune on 10k labeled pairs).

2) Retrieval + reranker settings to evaluate (we'll provide configs):
   - Retriever: Dense ANN with embedding model 'redwood-embed-small', k=100, shard by product domain.
   - Reranker: Cross-encoder re-score top-100 -> top-5, tuned for precision@1.
   - Grounding metric: grounding_rate (answers with a top-1 citation that contains >80% overlap with source passage), hallucination_rate, MRR@5, precision@1.

3) Prompting / eval assets:
   - We'll share an initial prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v2.json) and suggested instruction templates for short/long answers.
   - We'll run a benchmark suite across your KB slices (support articles, internal product guides) and return a summary report and per-prompt regression alerts.

Attached: a short evaluation stub (ACME_RAG_eval_report_v1.pdf) and the prompt set we discussed. Also linking the eval dashboard so you can review preliminary metrics: https://redwood-eval-dashboard.internal/acme/rag/summary

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood: run full eval (retriever+k=100, reranker cross-encoder, 3 model candidates) and return a detailed report + recommended config. Target turnaround: 5 business days.
- ACME: share a representative KB export (S3/Drive link) and a prioritized prompt set (top 200 queries).
- Schedule: 30-min sync next week to review results and align on mutual action plan.

Can you confirm S3 link for the KB export and preferred times for a review next week?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0127

---
Attachment: ACME_RAG_eval_report_v1.pdf (summary of initial sanity checks)
Attachment: acme_prompt_set_v2.json (200 example prompts)

Subject: Re: ACME RAG eval - post-call recap & next steps

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Technical notes on the eval run and the configs we'll use (also attached YAML + prompt set):

- Eval environment: We can run the eval inside your VPC via our Private offering (preferred) so no data leaves your network. If you prefer hosted, we'll accept a scrubbed subset.
- Retriever config (attached retriever_config.yaml): dense-embedding (redwood-embed-small), index sharding by domain, k_search=100, candidate_filter: metadata.product in {payments, billing}.
- Reranker: cross-encoder (distil-cross-enc-bert) fine-tuned on your FAQ pairs; scoring threshold tuned to maximize precision@1.
- Model inference profiles: we'll capture per-token latency and token-cost estimates for each model. Expect roughly: LLaMA-2-13B (quant) -> 0.6ms/token; RedLlama-70B-q4 -> 1.8ms/token (varies by hardware).
- Grounding checks: we run two automated checks — citation_overlap (Jaccard over tokenized spans) and source-verifiability (anchor phrase present in top-k doc). We'll report grounding_rate and hallucination_rate per prompt template.

Attachments: retriever_config.yaml, acme_prompt_set_v2.json, ACME_RAG_eval_report_v1.pdf (placeholder).

I'll kick off the run as soon as we have the S3 presigned link (or access inside your VPC).

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

2) Cost estimate (very rough): for a 5k-query run with k=100 and a cross-encoder rerank step, estimate: 
   - LLaMA-2-13B quant baseline: ~$1.2k total (mostly compute + embedding ops)
   - RedLlama-70B-q4 production candidate: ~$4.5k total (higher GPU time + reranker costs)
